params.question: Prevention of surgical site infection rests on three foundational measures. Which combination correctly identifies all three?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prophylactic antibiotics are a valuable adjunct but are not one of the three foundational measures. The correct triad is sterilization of instruments, antisepsis of skin, and a maintained sterile field.

answers.text: Antisepsis, hand hygiene, and antibiotic wound irrigation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hand hygiene is part of antisepsis, but this list is incomplete and incorrectly adds antibiotic irrigation. The triad is sterilization of instruments, antisepsis of skin, and a maintained sterile field.

answers.text: Sterilization of instruments, antisepsis of skin, and a maintained sterile field

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Sterilization eliminates microbes from instruments, antisepsis reduces skin flora, and a sterile field prevents re-contamination during surgery — each targets a different link in the contamination chain.

answers.text: Sterile draping, post-operative dressing, and pre-operative fasting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Draping contributes to the sterile field but is only one component. Post-operative dressing and fasting are not among the three foundational measures: sterilization, antisepsis, and a maintained sterile field.

overallFeedback.feedback: The three pillars are sterilization of instruments, antisepsis of skin, and maintenance of a sterile field — each targets a different link in the contamination chain.
Correct. These three measures form an unbroken chain that keeps microorganisms away from the operative field.

interactions.label: A hot-air oven at 160 degrees Celsius is preferred over an autoclave for certain

params.question: A hot-air oven at 160 degrees Celsius is preferred over an autoclave for certain items. Which property of those items makes dry heat the better choice?

answers.text: They are contaminated with bacterial spores that resist moist heat

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Moist heat is actually more effective against spores than dry heat, denaturing proteins faster through direct heat conduction via water. Dry heat is chosen because certain items would be damaged by moisture.

answers.text: They would be damaged by moisture in the autoclave

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Items such as glassware, powders, and certain sharp instruments can be damaged by moisture. Dry heat avoids this by sterilising through hot air at 160°C for one hour.

answers.text: They are too large to fit inside a standard autoclave chamber

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Item size is a practical consideration but not the reason dry heat is preferred. The key factor is that certain items would be damaged by the moisture present in an autoclave.

answers.text: They require a higher sterilization assurance level than moist heat provides

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Moist heat is actually more efficient than dry heat at the same temperature. Dry heat is chosen when items cannot tolerate moisture, not because it provides greater assurance.

overallFeedback.feedback: Dry heat is chosen for items like glassware, powders, and sharp instruments that would be damaged by moisture in the autoclave. The choice of method always depends on what the item can tolerate.
Correct. The choice of sterilization method is dictated by what the instrument or item can tolerate — moisture-sensitive items go to the hot-air oven.

interactions.label: An incision placed parallel to Langer's lines heals with a finer scar. Which rea

params.question: An incision placed parallel to Langer's lines heals with a finer scar. Which reason best explains this?

answers.text: Langer's lines mark zones of increased blood supply to the skin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Langer's lines represent the orientation of least skin tension, not zones of blood supply. The finer scar results from reduced tension pulling across the wound edges.

answers.text: Parallel incisions avoid all major cutaneous nerves and vessels

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While a good incision respects nearby nerves and vessels, Langer's lines do not map nerve-free zones. Their advantage is that they mark the direction of lowest skin tension.

answers.text: Langer's lines correspond to the thinnest regions of the dermis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Langer's lines reflect the orientation of collagen fibres and skin tension, not dermal thickness. The scar is finer because the wound closes under lower tension.

answers.text: The wound edges experience less tension, resulting in less gaping

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Langer's lines mark the direction of least skin tension. An incision parallel to them gapes minimally, closes under low tension, and heals into a finer, flatter scar.

overallFeedback.feedback: Langer's lines mark the direction of least skin tension. An incision parallel to them gapes less, closes under lower tension, and heals into a finer, flatter scar.
Correct. Understanding Langer's lines helps plan incisions that close under minimal tension and heal with less scarring.

interactions.label: Vicryl and Prolene differ on both classification axes of suture materials. Which

params.question: Vicryl and Prolene differ on both classification axes of suture materials. Which statement correctly describes how?

answers.text: Vicryl is absorbable and braided; Prolene is non-absorbable and monofilament

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Vicryl breaks down over weeks (absorbable) and its braided structure knots well but can wick fluid. Prolene persists long-term (non-absorbable) and its single smooth strand passes cleanly through tissue with minimal bacterial harbouring.

answers.text: Vicryl is non-absorbable and monofilament; Prolene is absorbable and braided

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This reverses both properties. Vicryl is absorbable (breaks down in tissue) and braided; Prolene is non-absorbable (persists for long-term strength) and monofilament.

answers.text: Both are absorbable, but Vicryl is braided while Prolene is monofilament

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prolene is non-absorbable — it persists in tissue for long-term strength. Only Vicryl is absorbable. They also differ in filament structure: Vicryl is braided, Prolene is monofilament.

answers.text: Both are non-absorbable, but Vicryl is monofilament while Prolene is braided

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vicryl is absorbable, not non-absorbable, and it is braided, not monofilament. Prolene is the non-absorbable monofilament suture.

overallFeedback.feedback: Vicryl is absorbable (breaks down over weeks) and braided (knots well but can wick fluid). Prolene is non-absorbable (persists for long-term strength) and monofilament (smooth passage, fewer bacteria).
Correct. Understanding both axes for each suture helps you match the right material to the tissue type and required healing duration.

interactions.label: Converting a laparoscopic procedure to open surgery indicates a failure of surgi

params.question: Converting a laparoscopic procedure to open surgery indicates a failure of surgical technique.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The narration emphasises that when an operation cannot be completed safely by the laparoscopic approach, converting to open surgery is sound judgement, not failure. Patient safety always takes priority.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The narration states explicitly that converting to open surgery when an operation cannot be completed safely is sound judgement, not failure. Patient safety always takes priority over completing a procedure laparoscopically.
